# Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 86 (Bi-Vb Pc86)

**ID:** Bi-Vb Pc86

**Title (English, SuttaCentral):** 86. Wearing a hip ornament
**Title (English, from literature):** Wearing a hip ornament

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Saṅghāṇi Sutta* (Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 86) sets forth the rule that a nun who wears a decorative hip ornament (*saṅghāṇi*) commits an offense of expiation (*pācittiya*) [SuttaCentral; Hüsken 1997]. In her study of the Theravāda nun's Vinaya, Ute Hüsken observes that this rule likely addresses a decorative belt worn specifically by laywomen, accounting for the absence of an equivalent rule in the monks' Vinaya [Hüsken 1997]. While ordinary waistbands (*kāyabandhana*) worn over the robes were obligatory for both monks and nuns, simpler hip-threads (*kaṭisuttaka*)—though prohibited for monks in the *Cullavagga*—are permitted to nuns within the non-offense clause (*anāpatti*) of this rule [Hüsken 1997]. The text has been translated into English by Bhikkhu Brahmali [SuttaCentral].

Curated parallels for this rule in the Theravāda tradition include the *Bhikkhunī Pātimokkha* (Pācittiya 86) and the *Bhikkhunī Parivāra* (Pācittiya 86), alongside Chinese Vinaya parallels in the Dharmaguptaka (*Lzh Dg Bi Vb Pc 156* and its Pātimokkha counterpart) and Mahīśāsaka (*Lzh Mi Bi Vb Pc 157* and its Pātimokkha counterpart) traditions [SuttaCentral]. Machine text-reuse analysis by DharmaNexus records 214 shared passages across 73 Pali texts, showing extensive formulaic overlaps with sections in *Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Saṅghādisesa 3* (§1.11–1.19.1), as well as adjacent and related nun's Pācittiya rules such as Pc 87, Pc 89, Pc 50, and Pc 84 [DharmaNexus]. In addition, DharmaNexus identifies 18 cross-language matches with the Tibetan *Bhikṣuṇīvinayavibhaṅga* (D0005) [DharmaNexus].
